title: Peloton Authorizes $300 Million Share Repurchase Program
summary: Peloton Interactive's board authorized a buyback of up to $300 million of its Class A stock, funded with cash on hand, after a debt refinancing.
body_markdown:
The release states that there is no guarantee as to the exact number of shares, if any, that will be repurchased, and that the program does not obligate Peloton to acquire any specific number of shares. The program may be suspended, modified or discontinued at any time at the company's discretion. The release does not give an end date for the program.


"Through disciplined execution, Peloton has built a robust balance sheet and a strong engine for generating free cash flow," said Chief Financial Officer Sid Thacker. He said the program, alongside the refinancing, allows the company to deliver more value to shareholders "while retaining sufficient capital to further invest in our product roadmap and market expansion."


## Why It Matters for PTON


The company said the authorization follows its recently completed debt refinancing. In a[separate release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1639825/000163982526000052/pton-8xkex991pressrelease.htm) dated Friday, November 20, 2026, Peloton said it completed a $900 million global refinancing that reduced overall debt and extended debt maturities. It raised $700 million from new and existing investors through an upsized private offering of senior secured notes due 2032, entered into a new $200 million five-year revolving credit facility led by Goldman Sachs that replaced its existing $100 million facility, and repaid all term loans outstanding under its existing $1 billion five-year term loan facility, which it terminated.
